skill_traces.query:
Andrew: Hey, Audrey! I can't wait for the weekend. My girlfriend, Toby and I are going camping. It's been forever since I've been in nature.
Audrey: That's awesome! That must be fun! I just started agility classes with my pups at a dog park. It's awesome to watch them learn and build relationships with other dogs. Seeing them face and conquer challenges really warms my heart.
Andrew: Wow it's amazing to watch them grow together. They look so cool overcoming obstacles like that. Impressive stuff!
Audrey: Thanks! They've come a long way. They have so much fun with it, it's a great physical and mental workout. I take them to the park twice a week for practice - it's been a great bonding experience.
Andrew: Awesome! You're having fun with them and keeping them busy - how's that going? Btw look at the trail that I was just at. Cool right?
Audrey: It's been tough at times, but overall it's going great. We're all growing together. Check out this pic of us on a trail hike!
Andrew: Wow, nice hike! How long was the trail?
Audrey: The hike took us two hours and it was stunning! We saw lots of amazing views and it was great to explore nature.
Andrew: That sounds awesome! Being able to just be in nature and appreciate it is really cool. I wish I could do that more often.
Audrey: Nature really refreshes you, right? It's nice to appreciate all the beauty around us. Are there any outdoor activities you enjoy lately?
Andrew: Well for me hiking is the best. Being out in nature with all the trees and fresh air always refreshes me. Reaching the top of a challenging trail is amazing too - it feels like all worries just vanish when you get to the top.
Audrey: Yeah, totally. It's like you've achieved something and all worries just fade away. Nature is pretty special, huh?
Andrew: Yeah, nature really calms me down and relaxes my mind. It's like a break from the craziness of city living.
Audrey: Yeah! It's a refuge from the busy city life and it's even better when you can share it with someone special. My pets have been my good ol' buddies during all the tough times! They make me so happy and I love them so much.
Andrew: Agreed! Sharing something you enjoy with someone is great. Plus, those types of bonds bring loads of joy and love.
Audrey: Yeah, humans and animals have a cool connection. They bring us so much joy and love. I'm blessed to have my furry friends in my life. They're my companions and always make my day better.
Andrew: They're pretty lucky to have you as their owner. Hoping for the day I can have such a deep bond with Toby and experience that special bond too.
Audrey: Yeah they really mean the world to me. Btw, I never really asked, what breed is Toby?
Andrew: He's a German Shepherd - they're so smart and loyal! What do you think?
Audrey: German Shepherds are indeed awesome! They are super loyal and smart. You'll have an amazing connection with one!
Andrew: I hope so! I shold take him hiking with me, they would be great hiking buddies, so smart and loyal.
Audrey: Yep! German Shepherds are known for their loyalty and smarts. They love new journeys and would love exploring the outside with you. I can totally see you and your pup conquering trails together!
Andrew: Yeah, having someone who enjoys similar things would be great for hiking. Do you have any advice for city-dwellers that owns a pup?
Audrey: My advice would be to make sure you have enough time and energy for a pup - they need lots of attention and walks! Especially for a German Shepherd like Toby, he'll need to offset a lot of energy.
Andrew: Thanks for the advice! I'll definitely keep that in mind. I want to make sure I'm not limiting Toby's growth but not taking him out not enough.
Audrey: No worries, Andrew! It's important to be prepared and give a pup the love it deserves. Good luck with Toby!
Andrew: Thanks! Gotta take Toby out for a small hike at the local trail. Ttyl!

nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explicitly states how they view a person, pet, or group (e.g., 'pets are family', 'feel like family'), during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a user explicitly declares how they view someone or something (e.g., 'pets are family', 'my little family', 'feel like family', 'as a friend'), create a separate profile or relationship memory capturing that view, even if the message also contains event details like photos or activities.
Use memory kind 'relationship' when the statement defines a connection between the speaker and the subject; otherwise use 'state' or 'preference' for attitudes and values.
Apply to both first mentions and repeated mentions across sessions; record the view as a durable memory rather than folding it into an event memory.
Only extract when the framing is explicit or strongly implied; do not infer relationships from generic pleasantries, compliments, or small talk.

nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explicitly states how often they do a recurring activity, extract a durable memory with the activity and frequency.
content: During extraction, when a user explicitly states the frequency of a recurring activity (including colloquial phrases like 'very often', 'all the time', 'a couple times a week'), create a candidate memory capturing both the activity and the frequency.
Use memory kind 'state' for habitual routines and 'event' for scheduled recurring occurrences; resolve relative time from the message timestamp.
During CRUD, if a matching memory for the same activity already exists, UPDATE or MERGE it rather than adding a duplicate.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Statements of Personal Significance
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user says an object, photo, or item reminds them of someone or something, or has personal meaning.
content: During extraction, when a user describes an object, photo, or item as reminding them of someone or something ('reminds me of', 'makes me think of', 'means ... to me'), create a candidate state memory capturing the connection.
Record who is reminded (the speaker), the object, and what it reminds them of (person, feeling, or value) in the speaker's own words.
Treat such statements as durable personal facts even though they are phrased as effects or feelings, not as direct assertions; extract at most one memory per statement.
